description: What a memory record is. Status is deliberately absent: whether a record still holds is a judgment (questions.v1), not a stored field. Storing it would make model swaps unmeasurable.

record_id.rule: "rec_" + first 24 hex chars of sha256 over the canonical body {text, source, at, scope}

text.note: The decision or constraint, standalone. Not a conversation excerpt.

source.note: Which agent, tool, or human wrote it. Free-form for v1; identity arrives only if the relay goal is ever revived.

scope.note: Where the claim applies (service, repo, environment). Structural label only.

prev_hash.rule: sha256 hex of the previous record's canonical body; genesis is 64 zeros
prev_hash.note: Local tamper-evidence. A chain held by one party is a log, not a proof; this is deliberate and cheap.

absent_by_design_rationale: Every field above was a stored judgment in the legacy runtime. Here they are re-derivable at any time by running questions.v1 against the record set, which is what makes cross-model comparison possible. Re-adding any of them is a v2 design change and must say why the judgment is no longer trusted.
migration_note: The legacy ClaimStore stays readable and untouched. Migration is export-to-records, one record per current claim; statuses are not carried over because they will be re-judged.
